sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Specialty Fresh Bakery Master Franchise and Central Kitchen Ops

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (national unitary jurisdiction; registrations effectuated through the Registro Público de Panamá, Panama City)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law tradition (Napoleonic origin) with strong notarial and public registry formalism; Private Interest Foundations (PIFs) are governed by the lex specialis Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995, modeled on Liechtenstein-style private foundations; commercial companies are governed by the Código de Comercio and Ley No. 32 de 1927.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States – Republic of Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 31 October 2012; includes an investment chapter with investor-state protections)
Panama – United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (1985)
Panama – Kingdom of the Netherlands Bilateral Investment Treaty (2002)
Panama – Federal Republic of Germany Bilateral Investment Treaty (1989)

Panama – People's Republic of China: no bilateral investment treaty is currently in force; relations are governed by the 2017 Memorandum on Economic and Trade Cooperation, and PRC investors are advised to structure through a jurisdiction covered by an active Panama BIT if treaty protection is desired

Framework Agreement for FATCA implementation with the United States (2014), Law No. 76 de 2019 aligning Panama with OECD/Global Forum transparency standards, and Panama's membership in the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on BEPS

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Consolidated AML/CFT framework: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (Ley 23/2015), as amended by Ley No. 70 de 2019, Ley No. 129 de 2020 and Executive Decree No. 335 de 2021, regulando la Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF); final beneficial owner disclosure: Ley No. 70 de 31 de enero de 2019 and its implementing regulations on the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF), administered by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI); Private Interest Foundation instrument: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995, as amended by Ley No. 21 de 2017; corporate/registry framework: Ley No. 32 de 1927 and the tariff and procedural rules of the Registro Público de Panamá.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Charter (Acto de Dotación) and private Regulations (Reglamento)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Judicial Circuit of Panama (Notario Público de la Ciudad de Panamá)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (not required domestically; public registration at the Registro Público confers conclusive authenticity; notarized and apostilled copies are prepared for foreign banks and counterparties)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Founder's passport copy and UBO due diligence identity evidence (PRC citizen)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: People's Republic of China notary public (公证处) plus notarization chain and PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or authorized provincial Foreign Affairs Office apostille
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961; in force for the PRC since 7 November 2023)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Chinese franchisor's Business License / Certificate of Incorporation with unified social credit code (营业执照)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) or local Administration for Market Regulation of the PRC, with apostille by PRC MFA

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Spanish translation of the PRC founding documents and UBO declaration, executed before a Panamanian authorized public translator (traductor público autorizado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian authorized public translator registered with the Registro de Traductores Públicos Autorizados, ratified before a Panamanian Notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal Panamanian notarial authentication (no additional consular legalization if the underlying documents already bear the Hague Apostille)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement and pre-incorporation screening of the Founder, Council Members (Miembros del Consejo), the Protector (Protector de la Fundación), the Resident Agent and all explicitly or presumptively identified beneficiaries against: (i) OFAC SDN and consolidated US sanctions lists; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iii) EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (iv) Panama's UAF list of watched persons (Listado de Observados) and any domestic terrorist watchlist; (v) INTERPOL diffusion notices; and (vi) adverse-media/negative-news screening. PEP status must be identified at any level of public office and triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification and senior-management approval. The foundation's resident agent and law firm must retain CDD/EDD records for a minimum of five years following termination of the business relationship, per Ley 23/2015 and UAF regulations.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.aml_risk_override_notes: ISIC 5610 specialty bakery franchising is classified as Low_Risk_Standard for banking and AML purposes; however, the panama PIF will hold the master royalty and franchise intellectual property, so the resident agent must still perform full UBO piercing to the Chinese natural-person founder(s) and name each controlling person in the confidential RUBF filing, notwithstanding any nominee council appointment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — electronic services portal for denomination consultation and reservation (Dirección General de Denominaciones, Marcas y Derechos de Autor), integrated with the PANAMÁ EMPRENDE one-stop shop for commercial incorporation filings.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish is the mandatory registration language. Foundation denominations must be expressed in Latin characters and must include the term 'Fundación' or 'Foundation' to indicate legal form. Chinese ideographic brand names are not acceptable in the corporate denomination and must be romanized using Spanish-readable transliteration on the Registry; the Chinese-character chinagraphic brand may separately be protected through trademark filing before the DIGERPI (Dirección General del Registro Industrial). Denominations that are identical, homophonous, or confusingly similar to an existing registered company, foundation, trademark or government entity are rejected.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco / Bank / Savings / Caja de Ahorros
Valores / Securities / Bolsa / Stock Exchange / Fondo de Inversión / Mutual Fund
Financiera / Finance Company / Casa de Cambio
Panamá / República de Panamá / Estado de Panamá / Zona Libre de Colón (when implying state sponsorship)
Ministerio / Embajada / Consulado / Consejo / Autoridad (official-body suggestive denominations)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On presentation of the official rejection notice (avisos negativos), the applicant may: (i) request a written reasoning of the denial; (ii) file a 'recurso de reconsideración' before the Director General of the Registro Público within five (5) working days of notification, under the administrative procedure code Ley No. 38 de 2000; (iii) if reconsideration is denied, file a 'recurso de apelación' before the Pleno of the Registro Público within five (5) further working days; (iv) concurrently file a substitute name reservation to avoid delaying incorporation; and (v) after exhaustion of administrative remedies, seek judicial review before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia. Administrative silence for more than thirty (30) calendar days is treated as constructive denial for appeal purposes.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted and normal for the Private Interest Foundation, which is an asset-holding and IP-royalty vehicle: the law requires only a Panama resident agent with a fixed physical address, which serves as the registered office. The foundation is not required to maintain employees, premises or independent equipment. By contrast, the underlying Panama operating entity for bakery outlets and the central kitchen must maintain a physical commercial establishment with municipal operating license, Ministry of Health (MINSA) food-safety registration and labor health approvals; virtual office status is not permissible for the actual production and retail units.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For the PIF itself: low — estimated below 5% cumulative probability during the first two (2) years, with on-site presence limited to supervisory inspections by the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros (SUINF) or UAF only upon AML compliance triggers or suspicious activity reporting. For the franchised bakery outlets and central kitchen: high — estimated above 80% probability within the first twelve (12) months of operation owing to mandatory MINSA health-sanitation inspections and municipal commercial license verification.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.commercial_substance_substance_mapping: The PIF must demonstrate economic substance solely as the franchisor/licensor of the Chinese pastry chain master franchise, receiving Master_Royalty_Wire payments on a territorial-tax basis; intercompany royalty rates must be set at arm's length and memorialized in a franchise sub-license agreement with the Panama operating entity to withstand DGI transfer-pricing scrutiny and potential OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework substance requirements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and denomination no-objection search (three alternative names) at the Registro Público de Panamá
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Dirección General de Denominaciones)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff and prevailing market service fee of the resident agent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Panamanian market benchmark for private interest foundation formation (fixed-fee legal drafting)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff based on the foundation's initial patrimony (appr. US$250 to US$500 for standard capitalization; budgeted at minimum)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent first-year service fee including registered office address, constitution maintenance, and registry correspondence handling
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panama law firm acting as resident agent (agente residente)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing annual market benchmark for low-risk private interest foundation client accounts

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Final Beneficial Owner (RUBF) initial filing and UBO profile preparation with the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and resident agent compliance desk
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fee under Ley No. 70 de 2019 and implementing executive decree, passed through with agent compliance tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PRC notary public, PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs or authorized provincial Foreign Affairs Office, Panamanian authorized translator, and notarial ratification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document market benchmark (approximately US$25 to US$80 per apostille and US$60 to US$120 per translated page), aggregated for a standard bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Retained Panamanian international business and AML compliance counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed professional fee per the prevailing market benchmark for stage-one due diligence and compliance opinions

stage_1.qualitative_residual_risk_assessment: Low residual AML/CFT risk for the proposed PA_PIF as an IP-holding and royalty-collection vehicle integrated with ISIC 5610 specialty bakery franchise operations, subject to completion of full UBO piercing to the Chinese natural persons, mandatory PEP/sanctions screening, filing on the RUBF, and maintenance of the foundation's financial and registry records with the resident agent. The principal compliance anchors are: (i) the 25% UBO disclosure threshold under Ley 70/2019; (ii) the Hague Apostille chain for all PRC-origin identity and corporate documents; (iii) name clearance at the Registro Público within the 30-day reservation window; and (iv) registration of a licensed resident agent with physical office presence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Private Interest Foundation Law (Ley No. 25 de 12 de julio de 1995), Article 1 (definition), Article 2 (registration), Article 8 (registered agent), Articles 18-19 (Foundation Council powers), Article 23 (secretary), Article 24 (supervisory board); implementing Executive Decree No. 4 of 29 January 1996.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Pacto Fundacional / Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (Foundation Charter executed as a Notarial Founding Deed)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The PIF statute imposes no mandatory minimum foundation endowment; a nominal founding asset of USD 10 is legally sufficient. No escrow account or capital deposit requirement exists at the Registry, but Panama AML Law 23 of 2015 and correspondent-bank due diligence require the beneficial owner and the initial endowment to be documented.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 1. The undersigned Foundation Council, having been designated in the Founding Deed and acting under Articles 18 and 19 of Law 25 of 1995, unanimously resolves: (1) The Founder’s subscription is accepted; the initial endowment of USD 10 is deemed paid-in and credited to the Foundation’s assets. (2) The registered office is adopted as the address stated in the Founding Deed, with the appointed resident agent, as the official address for all notices and service. (3) [Name] is appointed President and [Name] is appointed Secretary/Treasurer, each empowered to administer assets, open bank accounts, and sign binding documents. Thus approved in Panama City.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability clearance and founder instructions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Departamento de Nombres, then intended Panamanian Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the three preferred foundation names in Spanish via the licensed Panamanian notary/attorney to obtain a negative-name certificate or name adequacy check. Ensure the chosen name does not conflict with existing companies, trademarks, or protected official names. Secure Founder and Foundation Council instructions in writing.
required_dossiers: Signed engagement letter with Panama resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, refile the application with the alternates provided; no new state fee is charged when the alternate is in the same submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the Founding Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panamanian Notary Public (Notaría Pública del Circuito) in Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Pacto Fundacional in Spanish in accordance with Law 25 and have all founding council members and the Founder execute the deed before a Panamanian notary. If a Founder is offshore, sign a notarized and apostillized power of attorney naming a local attorney-in-fact. Verify that the deed contains registered agent acceptance, asset declaration, bylaws, and council appointments.
required_dossiers: Final Spanish text of the Founding Deed
Consent letters of Foundation Council members
Power of attorney or direct execution evidence
Proof of address and legal existence of Founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Notary has the remedy of re-execution: return for signature correction or replace defective clauses via private amendment protocolized before the same notary before filing at the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration and inscription at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado, Filing Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original protocolized notarial deed (or authorized certified copy) with the Sección de Fundaciones, accompanied by the Registry fee receipt and the registered agent’s confirmation. The Registry assigns a Folio Real and inscribes the foundation and its council members. Request a stamped certificate evidencing the inscription date.
required_dossiers: Original protocolized Escritura Pública / certified copy
Registered agent acceptance for service of process
Treasury/ID of resident agent if requested
Power-of-attorney evidence for any filings by third party
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the examiner issues a defect notice (nota de objeción), the counsel must cure deficiencies or contest the objection by a written brief within 15 business days; if rejected, file the administrative appeal (recurso de reconsideración) with the General Directorate of the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of certificate of registration and foundation code
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Certifications Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, present a written request for a certified copy of the registered Founding Deed and the Certificate of Registration. Confirm the foundation’s legal existence under Panamanian law and obtain the tax number (RUC) if any local economic activity is to be carried out, or an operating certificate for nil-activity status.
required_dossiers: Resolution appointing representative to collect certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If certificate issuance is delayed, petition the Head of Certifications and where needed invoke the Administrative Due Process Law (Ley 38 de 2000) for expedite/quiet enjoyment after payment of statutory fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration governance, UBO and AML compliance file
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Resident Agent / Compliance Officer and Panamanian Financial Intelligence Unit (UAF) prescribed AML record keeping
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute and archive the First Board Resolution and Foundation Council minutes adopting the registered office and officers. Establish the UBO register at the registered agent’s office identifying settlor, council members, and protector if any, in line with Law 23 of 2015. Obtain council member consent and banking mandates if bank accounts are needed.
required_dossiers: Registered agent service agreement and fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AML/KYC review by the registered agent or UAF flags incomplete ownership data, supplement with sworn declarations and notarized source-of-funds evidence within the 30-day statutory cure window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) — Dirección General de Salud, Departamento de Regulación Sanitaria de Alimentos; municipal “Aviso de Operación” from the corresponding Municipio; centralized food production registrations are coordinated with the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permiso Sanitario de Funcionamiento / Registro Sanitario del Establecimiento de Alimento and municipal Aviso de Operación for the specialty bakery and central kitchen

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Cumplimiento Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Small retail bakery: Category I (Exempt from full EIA, subject to environmental registration); large central kitchen / chain production facility: Category II requiring a simplified Environmental Impact Study (EsIA) before operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet pH 6-9, BOD5 ≤ 250 mg/L, COD ≤ 500 mg/L, TSS ≤ 100 mg/L, fats/oils ≤ 30 mg/L; bakery oven exhaust must be captured with hoods to control combustion gases and VOCs in line with applicable World Bank IFC EHS and Panamanian technical standards; food waste shall be stored hygienically and disposed through licensed waste haulers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá for means of egress, fire detection and suppression; structural/load inspection and final occupancy clearance from the Municipio; occupational health and workplace safety registration with the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL); employer registration with the Caja de Seguro Social (CSS).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama. Official e-Tax portal: https://etax.mef.gob.pa; institutional website: www.dgi.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) constituted under Law 25 of 1995 is a legal person but is not automatically a registered taxpayer. Registration in the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) is compelled only when the foundation engages in Panama-source economic activity, trades through a local establishment, or elects to operate a commercial business. SOP for foreign-owned PIFs: (1) formalize the Foundation Charter before a notary and file it at the Registro Público, appointing a resident foundation agent; (2) access the e-Tax portal and file the 'Solicitud de Inscripción de Contribuyente' (DGI form 600-1) with the foundation charter, the agent's notarized acceptance, and identification of the founder and council members; (3) if the bakery franchise chain operates a central kitchen or master franchise office in Panama, complete the physical premises inspection and obtain a local patent (patente) from the corresponding Alcaldía as a precursor to RUC activation; (4) receive the RUC certificate with the 13-digit taxpayer number and enroll in the Social Security registry (CSS) if employees will be hired; (5) procure the digital signature certificate (firma digital) issued by authorized certification providers to activate electronic filing and electronic invoicing credentials. The DGI does not apply a check-the-box or look-through election at registration; the PIF''s fiscal identity is determined by the territorial-source classification of the activity it actually executes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Available statutory elections affecting the PIF and its bakery chain structure include: (a) the PIF's foundational election under Law 25/1995 to remain a private-interest vehicle holding assets solely abroad, keeping it outside the income tax net and outside ITBMS; (b) the election to convert the PIF's operation into an active commercial undertaking, which subjects its Panama-source revenue to corporate income tax; (c) the Optional Simplified Regime (Régimen Opcional Simplificado, ROS) for small taxpayers with gross annual turnover up to B/. 300,000; (d) the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime under Law 41/2007 and the Multinational Business Hub (SNM) regime under Law 254/2019 for managing royalty, franchise, and regional service income; and (e) Zona Libre de Colón and processing-zone classification for the manufacturing/re-export wing of the pastry chain, which confers import-duty exemption and ITBMS deferral on re-export. Hybrid mismatch elections are not separately codified; Panama's territorial system and absence of general anti-avoidance hybrid rules make the PIF's offshore-fee flows eligible for favorable treatment if danger of DGI re-characterization is managed through substance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (the Panamanian VAT system governed by Law 31 of 2007, as amended by Law 8 of 2010 and subsequent fiscal regulations)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Panama imposes no economically significant de minimis turnover threshold for mandatory ITBMS registration: every person carrying out habitual taxable commercial activity, transferring movable goods, rendering services in Panamanian territory, or importing goods is obliged to register and collect ITBMS from the first taxable event. Reference thresholds: (a) large taxpayers are classified above B/. 3,000,000 annual gross revenue for compliance supervision; (b) small taxpayers may elect the ROS only up to B/. 300,000 annual gross turnover; (c) micro taxpayers may access the simplified micro/small taxpayer regimes with stricter administrative caps; (d) imports are subject to ITBMS at the customs port irrespective of business volume. A bakery master franchise chain is thus registrable as an ITBMS collector from the first sale to a franchisee or end consumer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing has been phased in by DGI Resolution 201-3887 of 27 November 2019 and subsequent 2021–2023 amendments. All RUC holders must issue invoices through the e-Tax 'Facturación Electrónica' platform or authorized billing intermediaries, with real-time transmission to DGI servers for fiscal clearance. Each invoice receives a unique authorization key ('Clave de Fiscalización') and must display: the issuer's RUC, the digital fiscal stamp (sello digital/firma calificada), and a QR code. Point-of-Sale (POS) systems must integrate the DGI fiscal-control module and obtain online authorization for each sales transaction before the receipt is legally issued; daily closing summaries must be transmitted. Invoices lacking DGI validation are invalid, unable to support input VAT credits, and inadmissible as evidence for export zero-rating or refund claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% ITBMS is available when: (1) movable goods, including frozen or finished bakery products, physically depart the Panamanian customs territory via a valid customs export declaration; (2) services are rendered for use, consumption, or effect entirely outside Panama, or are supplied to non-resident beneficiaries who lack Panamanian sources, qualifying as 'export of services' under Law 31/2007; (3) goods are sold to the Zona Libre de Colón or processing-free zones where the sale is formally connected to a subsequent re-export; and (4) franchise/royalty income under the PIF's master franchise is structured as offshore services invoiced to non-resident franchisees through a Panamanian invoicing entity. Substantiation requires the invoicing entity to prove both exit/offshore use and receipt of payment in a manner consistent with the export's commercial terms; documentary preparation at the moment of issuance is critical because the DGI reviews the export file and the e-invoice together.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) processed in the SIDUNEA customs system, containing the DGI validation and customs digital release code
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export of the bakery goods
Commercial invoice issued through the electronic invoicing portal bearing the fiscal stamp, QR code, and authorization key
Packing list detailing product, units, weight, and value
Inward Remittance Certificate / supporting SWIFT or bank ledger record certifying receipt of the export proceeds
Phytosanitary or food-safety export certificate issued by the Panamanian sanitary authority (in addition to the destination-country import permits)
Certificate of origin or ATR-type form where treaty benefits or duty preferences are claimed
Free-zone transit and re-export authorization where goods pass through Zona Libre de Colón or a processing zone
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are systematically cross-checked by the DGI against the customs exit log, the e-invoice database, and banking/FX records. A false or unsupported claim triggers retroactive reassessment of ITBMS at 7% (or 10% if the good/service falls within the higher band), plus quarterly surcharges of 15%, and administrative fines from 100% to 300% of the omitted tax under Código Fiscal Articles 705 and 706. In aggravated evasion cases the matter is referred for criminal prosecution with possible custodial penalties. The DGI additionally can revoke the electronic invoicing authorization and suspend the RUC, operationally shutting down all franchise POS clearances and central-kitchen sales. Failure to evidence inward FX repatriation or to document an acceptable offshore use of the exported goods/services within the 180-day informational benchmark — a period the DGI favors in audit protocols, with reasonable extension only on documented commercial grounds — leads to re-characterization of the transaction as a taxable domestic supply and disallowance of the resulting refund credit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the banking and foreign-exchange supervising authority; Panama does not maintain a classic central bank or issue monetary policy, as the United States dollar is legal tender and the Balboa is a unit of account only.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital account; no exchange controls distinguish capital or current transactions. The U.S. dollar is freely usable, and the Balboa exists only as coinage. Profit remittances are unrestricted; no prior Central Bank or SBP approval is required. Any applicable taxes, such as capital gains or dividend withholding for territorial-source earnings, are assessed separately and do not block transfer of funds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory export proceeds surrender exists under Panamanian law. There are no statutory surrender timelines, no required conversion ratios into local currency, and no requirement to register export receipts with the SBP. Export proceeds may be retained in U.S. dollars or another convertible currency, credited to a Panamanian account, and used freely for payments abroad or repatriation of profits.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. Pure offshore fintech EMI entities not supervised by the SBP have limited viability for opening a full corporate account or executing significant transaction flows due to correspondent-bank de-risking. Panama's Financial Innovation Law (Law No. 320 of 2023) provides a sandbox regime, and only licensed fintech participants or banks partnering with regulated EMIs may provide treasury services. A rational structure is to use a licensed local bank as the primary clearing agent and a sandbox-approved fintech facilitator only for point-of-sale settlement and merchant wallet receipts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For Private Interest Foundations (PIFs), one physical interview with the foundation council member and the ultimate beneficiary, or a high-grade video-conference enhanced due-diligence session, is required by most panamanian banks. Several fully remote onboarding workflows are possible for Low-Risk business models if apostilled foundation documents, registered-agent certificates, passport copies, and valid proof of source of funds are provided. For a bakery master-franchise entity, the SBP expects a definitive identification of the foundation holder, the economic controllers, and the persons with signatory power. A fully digital opening is available but requires prior admission by the bank's compliance committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-transparent foundation ownership or silent beneficiaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Private Interest Foundation deed with beneficiary clauses; notarized and apostilled foundation charter; Certificate of Incumbency issued by Registered Agent; current list of Foundation Council members; signed waivers permitting the bank to perform full UBO verification; and an economic substance narrative identifying the bakery operating company as the ultimate beneficial interest.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Off-shore incorporator or shell-company risk from a third-country jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the valid registered-agent licence; incorporation certificates of any intermediate holding vehicles; legalized commercial extract from the jurisdiction of the founder; complete chain of ownership from PIF to bakery franchise entity; audited or reviewed financial statements of the bakery operating company; and clear source-of-wealth documentation for initial endowment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Political/Exposed Person (PEP) involvement in the foundation or unexpected material donor
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Final beneficial owner declarations on official bank forms; PEP status assessments with a candidate screening report; notarized affidavits of source of funds; tax returns of donors related to the endowment; independent third-party background-check evidence; compliance sign-off from the registered agent confirming that no sanctioned entity is a designated or incidental beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound wire originating from a cryptocurrency exchange or unregulated investment platform
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade history and withdrawal confirmations from the exchange; formal contribution agreement for the PIF endowment; sworn declaration proving non-anonymous origin; police-business license of the bakery chain; internal compliance memorandum showing the source of cryptocurrency liquidated on regulated venues; and proof of payment of Panamanian asset-transfer taxes or stamp duties, if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fast-food bakery retail cash-heavy and POS-related unusual transaction pattern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed sales ledger and daily closing report from all franchise locations; POS terminal service agreements and merchant acquiring contracts; centralized kitchen invoices; payroll records and social-security filings; Panamanian municipal operating license; tax filings and refund reports; and a letter from an external auditor confirming that no abnormal cash cycle is present.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foundation endowment and shareholder capital injections from abroad will be channelled by SWIFT MT103 priority transfers to a designated Capital Escrow Account maintained at a Top-Tier Panamanian bank. The beneficiary must include the full certified PIF name and the purpose field should state 'FOUNDATION INITIAL CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / SUBSCRIPTION TO PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION UNDER PANAMA LAW 25 OF 1995'. The remitter must appear uniformly on all corporate records. Beneficiary bank will require a legalized copy of the foundation deed, a certificate of legal existence, a registered-agent letter, the KYC acceptance form, and the bank's specific 'Confirmation of Source of Funds' executed by the contributor. Because Panama is dollarized, no foreign-exchange conversion occurs for USD->USD movement. For non-USD original currencies, the transferring bank will convert at market rate and communicate the SWIFT MT202 cover payment through a correspondent U.S. or Panamanian clearing bank. The inbound remittance should also include the IPT (Impuesto de Transferencias de Bienes Muebles y Prestación de Servicios) invoice number if the capital brings a taxable asset, or, where exempt, a letter from outside counsel listing the applicable exemption.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing for trade settlements is primarily performed through (a) SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfers for raw ingredients, franchise royalties, supplier invoices, and equipment deposits; (b) irrevocable at-sight commercial letters of credit (LC) confirmed by a U.S. or European correspondent for larger kitchen fixtures and central-kitchen machinery; and (c) ACH debits or payroll in Panama using the national clearing house accompanying the 'Cámara de Compensación' for local vendors and franchise operators. For CNY, EUR or other currency settlements, the Panamanian bank will issue MT103 US-treasury-backed messages via a New York or Hong Kong correspondent, with full SWIFT travel-rule fields. Trade payment instructions must identify the ISIC 5610 bakery master-franchise operating company as the remitter and the exact purchase order number, LC applicant, and product classification code. Commercial LCs will be issued against signed central-kitchen supply agreements, pro-forma invoices, and marine or air bills of lading; payment on sight occurs only after compliance authentication and ATA customs documents are received.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CNH OTC forward contracts executed under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with licensed SBP-supervised banks or their overseas affiliates
USD/CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) used specifically to hedge franchise-import vendor costs settled in offshore RMB without physical delivery to mainland China
USD/EUR cross-currency basis swaps for European kitchen equipment purchases and royalty remittances
USD/MXN or USD/local central-American NDFs for sub-franchise royalties from adjacent markets
OTC FX options, collars, and participating forwards with a licensed Panamanian bank on a non-speculative, hedge-only basis
Interest-rate and currency swaps where the underlying exposure is a funded business acquisition from a cross-border bakery manufacturer

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual legal-entity tax of the Private Interest Foundation (Impuesto Anual de Personas Jurídicas / annual PIF treasury fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance; solvency certificate noted by the Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March under the DGI-published payment calendar; a PIF may also follow the anniversary-month window established at registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge and 1% monthly interest after the due date; the DGI will block the issuance of the legal-entity solvency certificate; unpaid annual fees for two consecutive years expose the PIF to administrative strike-off by the Registro Público de Panamá.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation and UBO declaration update for the Private Interest Foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Resident agent and Dirección General de Ingresos – Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually reconfirmed with the resident agent before the franchise-tax due date, and updated with the RUBF within 15 business days after any change in the foundation council, protector, beneficiaries, or significant economic-interest holder.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties of USD 1,000 to USD 50,000 per registration; possible resident-agent suspension; the Registro Público de Panamá may strike off a PIF that lacks a compliant resident agent and updated UBO record.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return (Declaración Jurada de Renta) for any Panama-source business income of the bakery franchise or central kitchen
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 March for a 31 December fiscal year end; for any other fiscal year end, by the last day of the third month following the close of the fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 10% of the tax due plus 1% monthly interest; DGI may initiate forced collection, seizure of bank accounts, and administrative assessment after 12 months of non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is compulsory when the bakery chain generates annual gross receipts of USD 1,000,000 or more, or when total assets reach or exceed USD 2,000,000. A passive PIF treasury vehicle remains below this threshold unless it consolidates the operating bakery entity and its Panama-source activities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama for audited financial statements; IFRS for SMEs is permitted for smaller private interest foundations. Panama GAAP and cash-basis records may be maintained while the PIF does not meet the audit threshold.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The PIF has no share capital; changes in economic interest are effected through the Foundation Council. The resident agent must confirm the UBO schedule annually, covering the founder, foundation council members, protector and all beneficiaries, and must update the RUBF within 15 business days after any relevant transfer, replacement, or beneficial-interest modification.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Beneficiaries with economic interests
Register of Foundation Council Members and Officers
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500–USD 1,200 per year for a Panama licensed resident agent and registered office
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–USD 6,000 per year for the bakery chain if the audit threshold is met

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama operates a territorial income tax system. Foreign-source income is excluded from the Panamanian tax base. For onshore bakery franchise operations, no general statutory tax holiday is available; preferential regimes may apply only to licensed operators under the SEM (Multinational Headquarters), Free Zone, or City of Knowledge regimes. Depreciation and deductions follow the Panamanian Tax Code; certain accelerated allowances may be available for fixed assets used in the commercial kitchen and distribution network.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 101 – Declaración Anual del Impuesto Sobre la Renta (Personas Jurídicas), filed through the DGI electronic portal 'DGI en Línea' (portal.dgi.gob.pa).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 90 calendar days after the fiscal year-end. For calendar-year taxpayers, the statutory deadline is 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from Panamanian source, including bakery franchise sales, royalty streaming, management fees, and distribution revenue sourced to Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Panama Private Interest Foundation holding only foreign-origin passive income must exclude such foreign income; all Panamanian-source income must be declared even if billed offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating costs, franchisee support expenses, central kitchen overhead, payroll, rent, and allocated fees attributable to the production of Panamanian-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be directly linked to taxable Panama-source revenue; intercompany allocations must be substantiated by transfer pricing documentation and cannot exceed arm’s length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after allowable deductions and permitted NOL carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PIF with no active Panamanian commercial activity, enter zero; do not offset foreign-source losses against Panamanian tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable at 25% on net Panamanian-source taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% strictly to revenue sourced within the Republic of Panama; treaty benefits do not reduce Panama corporate income tax on Panama-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax credits, advance income tax payments, and credit carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot take personal tax credits against the PIF’s tax liability; only Panamanian tax withheld or paid by the entity itself may be credited.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers economic surcharges on the unpaid balance, administrative interest, and fines under the Código Fiscal (commonly from B/.10.00 to B/.5,000.00). Recurrent non-filing is prosecuted as tax evasion, leading to punitive fines and possible imprisonment of responsible directors.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 910 – Declaración Informativa de Precios de Transferencia y Operaciones con Partes Relacionadas, filed through DGI en Línea together with Form 101.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same statutory deadline as Form 101; a written extension may be requested prior to the due date, but approval is discretionary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the Panamanian entity and each related party involved in controlled transactions, including name, tax identification number, jurisdiction, and relationship type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fully identify all foreign shareholders of the PIF, including beneficial owners under the ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) register, and all foreign related franchisees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate related-party transaction values, broken down by category (royalties, interest, management fees, goods, services, financing), and the net contribution to Panamanian-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List only transactions that are recorded in the books of the Panama PIF or of its local franchise subsidiary; do not list transactions purely between foreign vehicles outside Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing method selection for each category of controlled transaction, plus the arm’s length range and comparability set.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the most appropriate Panamanian approved method; for low-risk royalty collection by a PIF, TNMM or CUP are common; any profit split method must be supported by detailed functional analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of whether a Local File or Master File is held, and whether the taxpayer is exempt from filing due to transaction thresholds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF that licenses IP to a Panamanian bakery chain must hold a Local File if the aggregate annual related-party transaction value exceeds the threshold; a Master File is required for consolidated group turnover above the higher threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Form 910, or filing an inaccurate return, exposes the taxpayer to transfer pricing adjustments and a penalty of up to 20% of the adjusted difference, plus interest; additional fines up to B/.5,000 and reputational sanctions apply.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (statutory rate on dividends paid to any shareholder; an alternative 5% rate applies where the distributing profits have already borne Panamanian corporate income tax at the full 25% rate and are separately identified in the reserves).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double taxation agreement (DTA), the non-resident shareholder must deliver to the Panamanian withholding agent (a) an official Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, normally within the preceding six months; (b) a completed DTA relief claim form; and (c) evidence verifying the legal and equitable ownership of the dividend. The withholding agent must retain these documents for six years and file the monthly withholding return applying the reduced treaty rate. Where the PIF is the legal owner of dividends but the domestic franchise entity is the payer, Panama will require proof of the foundation’s substance and beneficial ownership chain before granting treaty relief. No treaty reduction is available in the absence of a ratified DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on IP royalties paid to non-residents is 10%, while interest paid to non-resident lenders is generally subject to 5% withholding; interest paid to recognized foreign banks, export-credit institutions, and certain listed debt instruments may be exempt under the Panamanian Tax Code. DTA rates vary by jurisdiction and may reduce royalty and interest withholding, subject to the TRC administrative protocol.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and supporting transfer pricing study are mandatory where the aggregate annual related-party transactions exceed B/.250,000 (USD 250,000) or where gross annual revenue exceeds B/.1,000,000 (USD 1,000,000). A Master File is triggered when the consolidated group revenue exceeds B/.50,000,000 (USD 50,000,000).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Yes. Panama’s Economic Substance Regulations apply to PIFs and commercial entities performing geographically mobile activities, including intellectual property holding, distribution, financing, and service center functions. A bakery franchise PIF that holds trademarks and receives royalties from the local operating chain must demonstrate continuous economic substance: physical presence in Panama, personnel with appropriate qualifications, active board decisions, and operating expenditure proportionate to the income. Pure holding PIFs with no active intra-group management may be exempt if they do not conduct mobile businesses and simply hold shares and dividends; however, any active royalty licensing or central-kitchen management activities require substance reporting.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Panamanian-source sales from the local bakery franchise chain in Form 101, fabricating deductions, or remaining entirely unfiled for three consecutive fiscal years while cash-heavy operations generate substantial income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 50% to 100% of the evaded tax, penal interest, loss of tax clearance, seizure of bank accounts, and criminal prosecution under Panama’s Criminal and Tax Code. Criminal punishment may range from three to ten years’ imprisonment, disqualification from acting as a director, and forfeiture of assets traceable to the evaded funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may pierce the PIF’s corporate veil where the foundation is used as a mere instrument of tax evasion. Directors, trustees, and legal representatives are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, face civil restitution, travel bans, precautionary asset attachment, and imprisonment in case of intentional fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging unsupported royalties or management fees to the local bakery franchise, using a 30% royalty rate without a comparability analysis, failing to file Form 910, or refusing to produce a Local File when the annual related-party transaction threshold has been crossed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may reprice the controlled transaction, disallow excess deductions, impose a penalty of up to 20% of the transfer pricing adjustment, levy annual interest on the under-withheld or underpaid tax, and charge specific fines for non-filing of Form 910 (up to B/.5,000).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved the arbitrary pricing scheme can be held jointly and severally liable for the additional tax and penalties. During TP audits, responsible officers may be prohibited from leaving Panama and must appear before the tax court; intentional submission of materially false documentation may trigger criminal sanction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF solely as a mailbox for the bakery franchise’s royalties—without any physical office, employees, active bank account in Panama, local minutes of meetings, or evidence that core decisions are made in Panama—while claiming territorial exemption or treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Panama’s economic substance regulation exposes the entity to cumulative financial penalties up to USD 500,000, mandatory exchange of information with foreign tax authorities, loss of the PIF’s license, and strike-off from the registry after continued non-compliance. The DGI also denies treaty benefits from a hollow foundation and treats the income as Panamanian-source.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers and foundation founders who signed false substance declarations are personally liable to civil fines and damages. A travel ban may be imposed against foreign directors during a criminal investigation, and Panama’s cross-border cooperation can lead to extradition or placement on an Interpol notice for serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering Through Cash-Heavy Business
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Depositing daily bakery cash sales into PIF-controlled Panamanian bank accounts without proper UBO disclosure, using unregistered cashiers or currency exchangers, structuring payments to avoid banking thresholds, or using the Chinese pastry chain as a shell to facilitate illegal cross-border transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Panama’s Law 23 of 2015 (AML/CFT), licensed subjects face fines ranging from USD 100,000 to USD 2,000,000 per violation, suspension or revocation of licenses, closure of the local operations, criminal money-laundering penalties up to twelve years’ imprisonment, and forfeiture of laundered assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, trustees, and beneficial owners who knowingly allow money laundering through the PIF or the franchise chain incur personal criminal liability, travel bans, freezing of personal bank accounts, and confiscation of residential or commercial assets held through the foundation. The corporate veil is not recognized for illicit proceeds; principals may be prosecuted extraterritorially.
